    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Democrats' midterm election win has put the artificial intelligence trade in question, as voters clearly expressed opposition to the rapid buildout of data centers.
    • In this scenario, investors can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios to earn steady income.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Democrats' midterm election win has put the artificial intelligence trade in question, as voters clearly expressed opposition to the rapid buildout of data centers. The stock market could remain volatile amid AI trade concerns, macro uncertainties, and geopolitical tensions.

    In this scenario, investors can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios to earn steady income. However, the extensive universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as these experts assign ratings after in-depth financial analysis.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Viper Energy (VNOM) is a subsidiary of Diamondback and owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests, primarily in the Permian Basin. The company reported upbeat third-quarter earnings, supported by recent acquisitions and continued development activity from Diamondback and third-party operators. Viper confirmed a base cash dividend of 50 cents per share for Q3 2026, payable on Nov. 19. Based on the base and variable dividends announced over the past 12 months, VNOM's dividend yield stands at 5.7%.

    In a recent development, following the Q3 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper Energy stock with a price target of $61. The analyst noted that the company delivered solid Q3 results, with production, including oil and natural gas liquids, exceeding both TD Cowen and consensus estimates.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that the key patch was the announcement of two royalty acquisitions for $809 million in cash, including deferred consideration, and $82 million of newly issued shares.

    Given the recently unveiled base dividend hike, Bilkoski expects Viper to direct incremental free cash flow toward buybacks. While the acquisitions increase leverage, the analyst believes that Viper has enough capacity for opportunistic buybacks.

    Industry observers note that bilkoski noted that Viper has historically delivered one of the highest production per share growth profiles in his royalty coverage, but still trades at a notable discount to the royalty peer average and the company's historical FCF yield range. "In our view, its above-average growth warrants a higher valuation," said the analyst.

    Recent findings suggest that bilkoski ranks No. 525 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.80%. See Viper Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    Exxon Mobil (XOM) reported robust Q3 2026 profits, as its U.S. refineries boosted production to capitalize on the high diesel fuel prices sparked by the conflict in the Middle East. The oil and gas giant revealed a quarterly dividend of $1.07 per share, payable on Dec. 10, reflecting a 3.9% increase. This marks Exxon's 44th consecutive year of dividend increases. At an annualized dividend of $4.28 per share, XOM offers a yield of 2.53%.

    Impressed by the Q3 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Exxon stock and raised his price target to $193 from $180 to reflect higher downstream earnings, with the expectation of increased mid-cycle margins.

    Gabelman noted that the strength in Exxon's refining business continues to offset Middle East-related headwinds. He added that the company increased its ownership in LNG projects, which should reduce its Middle East concentration over time from 75% to 50% and lower the likelihood of diversification-focused mergers and acquisitions. Beyond LNG, Gabelman expects Exxon's growth in the 2030s to come from Guyana, Kashagan, Permian, and possibly Venezuela.

    Gabelman noted that Exxon announced a dividend hike of nearly 4% and aims to maintain buybacks at $20 billion for 2027. "The decision to maintain reduces the pro-cyclicality nature of the buyback," said the analyst.

    Sources indicate that gabelman ranks No. 347 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.90%. See Exxon Mobil Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that williams (WMB), which owns and operates energy infrastructure to deliver natural gas, reported strong third-quarter results. The tech giant announced a quarterly dividend of $0.525 per share, or $2.10 per share annualized, payable on Dec. 28. WMB offers a dividend yield of 3.09%.

    In reaction to the Q3 2026 results, CIBC analyst Robert Catellier reaffirmed a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $82. The analyst noted that Q3 results were essentially in line with expectations and reflected continued strength in execution across WMB's infrastructure portfolio.

    Catellier mentioned that Williams' Q3 performance was driven by higher transmission, storage, and power generation revenues, as well as contributions from the Momentum Midstream acquisition.

    Industry observers note that he noted that Williams maintained its full-year EBITDA guidance of $8.3 billion to $8.5 billion. In fact, results are tracking toward the higher end of the guidance range, backed by contributions from recently completed projects and the Momentum Midstream deal. WMB continues to target long-term EBITDA compound annual growth rate of at least 11% through 2030.

    Catellier expects WMB's long-term targets to be supported by incremental transmission and storage opportunities, including Transco's Southeast Supply Enhancement II project and an 84 MMcf/d expansion of the Garden Connector project.

    Sources indicate that catellier ranks No. 667 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 9.60%. See Williams Technical Analysis on TipRanks.

    Warren Buffett’s Record Cash Pile Is Sending Investors a Message About AI Stocks

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (743 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.
    • Despite a bull market, Warren Buffett spent his last years at Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.49%) (BRKB +0.41%) selling stocks and stockpiling cash.
    • However, the cyclically adjusted P/E (CAPE) ratio of 41 is near an all-time high, so Buffett may have merely been reacting to that metric or similar ones.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Will Healy – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Berkshire Hathaway ›.

    Despite a bull market, Warren Buffett spent his last years at Berkshire Hathaway (BRKA +0.49%) (BRKB +0.41%) selling stocks and stockpiling cash. The company's $377 billion in liquidity is close to a record and exceeds its approximate $346 billion in stock holdings. Many investors found this move perplexing, with Buffett selling stocks at a time when most other investors were buying.

    However, the cyclically adjusted P/E (CAPE) ratio of 41 is near an all-time high, so Buffett may have merely been reacting to that metric or similar ones. I believe Buffett is telling us something that may seem surprising but really is not, and it has nothing to do with hating artificial intelligence.

    Warren Buffett. Image source: Getty Images.

    Make no mistake, technology has long been part of Berkshire’s portfolio.

    According to recent reports, berkshire's largest investment has long been Apple (AAPL +1.90%). Despite the reduction in that position, it still accounts for around 23% of the company's holdings.

    In a recent development, moreover, both Buffett and his successor, Greg Abel, bought shares of Google's parent company, Alphabet (GOOGL +6.34%) (GOOG +5.88%). They made aggressive purchases in late 2025 and 2026, adding $10 billion of this AI stock in June alone. This is meaningful as Berkshire has made few aggressive buys in recent years. Between Alphabet's two tickers, it accounts for an additional 8% of Berkshire's holdings.

    Furthermore, until early 2026, Berkshire held a position in Amazon (AMZN +3.47%), a cloud pioneer and longtime AI innovator.

    Among these holdings and connections, AI accounts for around 31% of the Berkshire portfolio, so Buffett clearly wasn't avoiding it.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    The message Berkshire is sending about AI stocks is that they should be treated just like any other investment.

    Admittedly, Buffett was a longtime opponent of technology investing. But once he became convinced of its importance and likely permanence, he sought out tech investments and applied many of the same principles that led him to buy stocks such as American Express (AXP +1.72%) and Coca-Cola (KO -1.14%).

    Apple was one of the more notable investments. Apple consistently traded at P/E ratios below 20 when Berkshire did the bulk of its buying in the second half of the 2010s. This likely means Buffett bought the stock below its intrinsic value. Additionally, the economic moat built around its core product, the iPhone, and the company's strong free cash flows, probably also influenced the decision to buy.

    Many of the same characteristics appear to apply to Alphabet. It has often traded below 20 times earnings in recent years and maintains offerings with AI-supported moats like Google Advertising, Google Cloud, and the Android operating system. Alphabet has also stood out for strong free cash flows, even though its recent AI-related capital expenditures have led to outflows in recent quarters.

    Altogether, both Apple and Alphabet are, by most accounts, wonderful companies Buffett and his team bought at fair prices, and Greg Abel seems to be carrying that philosophy forward. Hence, little has changed with Berkshire's investment style; it just happens to be applied to AI in this case.

    In a recent development, buffett's message about AI is that there is no AI message. Although he and now Abel have taken large positions in leading technology companies, the Buffett investment philosophy remains the driving force behind Berkshire's stock purchases.

    The truth is he employed the same philosophy to buy Apple and Alphabet that he applied to his other major holdings earlier in his career. Fortunately for Berkshire, some AI stocks became the wonderful companies at fair prices that Buffett liked to find, and he made sure Berkshire capitalized on those opportunities.

    Sources indicate that knowing that, I believe the lesson here is that if one applies Buffett's philosophy to stocks across a multitude of industries, they have a better chance of earning market-beating returns. That approach is likely more crucial than whether a holding is an AI stock.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • It has been revealed that chip stocks, which have delivered incredible gains over the past four years amid the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, have taken a big beating lately.
    • Investors, however, will be looking for a turnaround in the stock's fortunes when it releases its fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter results on Dec.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Harsh Chauhan – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Broadcom ›.

    Broadcom (AVGO +3.00%) stock has been crushed in recent months, falling 35% from the 52-week high it reached on June 3, amid dwindling confidence in the semiconductor sector.

    It has been revealed that chip stocks, which have delivered incredible gains over the past four years amid the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, have taken a big beating lately. The hotter-than-expected inflation, a hawkish Federal Reserve, and the sustainability of the heavy spending on AI data center infrastructure have led investors to press the sell button and book profits. This explains why Broadcom has taken a big beating lately.

    Investors, however, will be looking for a turnaround in the stock's fortunes when it releases its fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter results on Dec. 9. Let's see if the upcoming quarterly results could indeed give Broadcom stock a much-needed boost.

    Recent findings suggest that broadcom has beaten Wall Street's earnings per share (EPS) expectations in each of the last four quarters. Broadcom's AI business has played a central role in its outperformance, which isn't surprising as it is the market share leader in custom AI processors, and is also benefiting from the booming demand for networking components.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    The company reportedly controls an estimated 60% of the fast-growing custom AI processor market, according to Counterpoint Research. Not surprisingly, Broadcom's shipments of custom AI processors increased by 3.5x year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. Meanwhile, its revenue from sales of AI networking components is also increasing at a solid pace, jumping 2.5x year over year in fiscal Q3.

    Broadcom expects $34.8 billion in fiscal Q4 revenue, an improvement of 93% from the year-ago period. That will be a significant jump over the 28% growth it delivered in the same period last year. The company's AI revenue is expected to have increased by 236% year over year in the previous quarter to $21.7 billion.

    However, Broadcom's revenue could exceed expectations. That's because the demand for its AI chips is exceeding supply. It has been working to secure additional supply, which is why its financial performance may be better than expected. Moreover, Broadcom sees phenomenal growth in its AI revenue over the next two fiscal years.

    It anticipates AI revenue will almost double in fiscal 2027 to $115 billion, compared with the fiscal 2026 estimate of $58 billion. What's more, it sees $230 billion in AI chip revenue in fiscal 2028. However, these estimates are based on the supply that it has already secured, which explains why Broadcom management noted on the September earnings call that it may increase guidance as it strengthens its supply chain.

    Sources indicate that on the other hand, the demand for optical networking components that Broadcom designs is "far surpassing supply out there in the industry." This supply shortage should ideally lead to higher prices for optical networking components, which is why Goldman Sachs estimates that optical networking revenue will increase from an estimated $15 billion this year to $154 billion in 2028. The investment bank also notes that an increase in average selling price (ASP) could boost the gross margins of optical component suppliers.

    All this suggests Broadcom's revenue and earnings could once again surpass Wall Street's expectations when it reports results next month. Additionally, the manufacturer has dropped enough hints that it could continue to upgrade its guidance as supply chain improvements materialize. As such, Broadcom's guidance may surpass expectations, setting the company up for a strong rally in December.

    Sources indicate that analysts predict a 71% jump in Broadcom's fiscal 2026 EPS to $11.65, well above the 33% average earnings growth estimated for S&P 500 companies. The chip designer is expected to post another solid 66% increase in EPS next year to $19.33, again exceeding the 17% jump that S&P 500 companies are expected to deliver. The fiscal 2028 EPS estimate is also quite impressive.

    AVGO EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts.

    It has been revealed that broadcom's forward earnings multiple of 16 is slightly lower than the S&P 500 index's forward earnings multiple of 18. This semiconductor stock should ideally be trading at a premium valuation due to its market-beating EPS growth. Assuming Broadcom trades at 25 times earnings after a year and its EPS reaches $19.33 in fiscal 2027 (based on the consensus estimate seen in the chart above), its stock price could reach $483.

    That implies a potential 54% jump in a year. Analysts, however, are more upbeat about Broadcom's performance, as its 12-month median price target of $522 implies 66% gains. All this suggests that Broadcom could be a solid buy ahead of its quarterly report, as strong results could supercharge the stock in December and pave the way for a much-improved performance in 2027.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 17, Nike (NKE +2.55%) concluded its first investor day meeting in nine years.
    • Elliott Hill, chief executive officer since October 2024, laid out a clear financial target that gives investors some hope.
    • Sources indicate that A profit outlook like this is encouraging, although the market doesn't see it that way today.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:05AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nike ›.

    On Nov. 17, Nike (NKE +2.55%) concluded its first investor day meeting in nine years. It came at a time of great uncertainty for the business. The brand's dominance is under threat. Revenue is declining. And profits have cratered.

    Elliott Hill, chief executive officer since October 2024, laid out a clear financial target that gives investors some hope. By fiscal 2031, Nike prepares to report adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $3.00 to $3.50. At the midpoint, this would be 106% higher than the $1.58 generated in fiscal 2026 (ended May 31).

    Sources indicate that A profit outlook like this is encouraging, although the market doesn't see it that way today. Shares fell 10% recently and were were down 46% in 2026. Investors are pessimistic, as the turnaround will take longer than expected.

    Assuming Nike is able to reach that adjusted EPS target in five years, here's what it could mean for the consumer discretionary stock.

    It's good for investors to first understand what exactly Nike intends to do to right the ship. The next few years are about resetting the playbook.

    Recent findings suggest that first, the business is narrowing its focus. The Full Stride Ahead strategy centers on five sports: running, training, global football, basketball, and outdoor. Together with sportswear and 23 priority countries, these areas are expected to drive more than 90% of the revenue growth through fiscal 2031 compared to fiscal 2027.

    According to recent reports, second, the three brands (Nike, Jordan, and Converse) don't change, despite speculation that Converse could be sold. Performance sports should deliver about $4 billion of the targeted $5 billion in added revenue versus fiscal 2027. Sportswear, which encompasses the firm's lifestyle-based apparel and footwear, supplies the other $1 billion.

    Third, Nike is pushing resources closer to priority countries and cities. Greater China, once a key growth engine, is dealing with recent challenges. India is a focal point now.

    Industry observers note that fourth, cost cuts need to do a lot of the heavy lifting. The Pace program targets about $2.5 billion in annualized savings by fiscal 2031, with impacts starting to be felt this fiscal year. That supports an operating margin goal of 12% to 14%, a massive improvement versus roughly 6% expected in fiscal 2027.

    In a recent development, timing is where it gets interesting. Management sees revenue shrinking this year and posting a "moderate" decline in fiscal 2028. Market-level growth isn't targeted until fiscal 2029. And investors will have to wait until the turn of the decade for accelerated growth.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Nike shares trade at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 16.5, based on trailing 12-month profits. Assume that the multiple holds steady for five years.

    It has been revealed that if Nike earns $3.25 per share in fiscal 2031, the midpoint of its target, the stock would climb 106% to roughly $71. A $10,000 investment today would be worth about $20,600, before dividends. That's more than a 15% annualized gain, well ahead of the long-term average of about 10% for the S&P 500 index (^GSPC +4.73%).

    It all sounds so easy. But the path is heavily back-loaded. Management guides for adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.35 in fiscal 2027. Getting from the fiscal 2027 midpoint to $3.25 requires 160% growth in four years. Investors would be paying to buy shares when profits are projected to fall in the near term.

    Sources indicate that the market has doubts, as evidenced by the stock's recent dip. At about 10.6 times the 2031 EPS target, the stock looks cheap on paper. Morgan Stanley (MS +4.18%) analyst Alex Straton called the goals optimistic.

    According to recent reports, that skepticism is fair. Turnarounds are defined by heightened uncertainty. The financial improvements might never show up. Or they could, but take a lot longer than expected. Nike is still a show-me stock with a lot to prove.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The San Antonio Spurs were without both Victor Wembanyama and De'Aaron Fox on Monday night.

    That didn't stop them from rolling past the Sacramento Kings.

    Industry observers note that wembanyama was ruled out of the Spurs' 123-107 win over the Kings due to back tightness, the team announced shortly before the game was set to tip off at the Golden 1 Center. Fox is dealing with a shin contusion, and was ruled out at the same time.

    While losing two star players for any contest is undoubtedly concerning, the two injuries were described as simply "bumps and bruises" by San Antonio Express-News' Jeff McDonald. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said both players are not expected to be sidelined long, but would not yet declare they would be ready to return for their NBA Cup matchup against the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday.

    The game against the Kings is the first that Wembanyama has missed all season. He's averaged 29.9 points, 12.3 rebounds and 3.9 blocks through the first 17 games of the season, all of which are career highs for the 22-year-old. He's fresh off a wild 50-point outing on Saturday night. Wembanyama outscored the New Orleans Pelicans starters by himself in the first half before rolling to a dominant win. It was his second 50-point game already this season, following a 52-point performance against the Dallas Mavericks earlier this fall.

    Fox has averaged 12.4 points and 5.8 assists per game this season. The 28-year-old is in his second full season with the Spurs, who landed him in a deal with the Kings during the 2024-25 campaign. Johnson noted Fox was injured when he was intentionally tripped by a Pelicans player.

    In a recent development, and though the Kings jumped up early in the opening frame, the Spurs rallied and led the entire second half to secure the 16-point win. Stephon Castle led the way with a near-triple-double. He had 28 points, 11 assists and eight rebounds on the night. Julian Champagnie added 22 points, and Luke Kornet finished with 18 points and 11 rebounds.

    According to recent reports, domantas Sabonis led the Kings with 20 points, 12 rebounds and eight assists in the loss, which dropped them to 2-15 on the season. Zach Lavine added 18 points, and De'Andre Hunter finished with 15 points and eight assists.

    The Spurs now hold a 15-3 record, which is tied for the best in the league with the Los Angeles Lakers. Though both Wembanyama and Fox should be back on the floor very soon, the team is clearly capable of holding things down without them when necessary.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The stock market's sell-off has put some high-quality companies back on my radar.
    • There's a difference, though, between a great tech giant and a great stock to buy right now.
    • So I've built a wish list of companies I'd happily buy and hold for a decade or longer, if the price is right.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Matt DiLallo – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:15AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Costco Wholesale ›.

    The stock market's sell-off has put some high-quality companies back on my radar. Last Friday, the S&P 500 fell 3.7% and closed more than 10% below its record high, officially entering a correction. Watching prices drop is uncomfortable, but corrections can also provide opportunities to buy outstanding businesses at better valuations.

    There's a difference, though, between a great tech giant and a great stock to buy right now. Some of the businesses I'd most like to own still trade at valuations that leave little room for error.

    So I've built a wish list of companies I'd happily buy and hold for a decade or longer, if the price is right. Here are five magnificent companies I'd love to own if they fall within my desired price range.

    Costco's (COST -0.39%) business model is hard to beat. Members pay an annual fee for access to low prices, and they renew at a remarkable rate: 89.8% worldwide. The tech giant has 84.1 million paid memberships, up 3.8% year over year. Its massive purchasing scale and continued growth (33 planned warehouse openings in fiscal 2027) should keep that flywheel turning in any economy.

    While Costco offers a great value proposition for customers, it's not nearly as attractive to prospective investors. Shares of the membership club have surged more than 20% over the past year and recently traded above $1,100 per share, near their all-time high, despite the market's correction. That has Costco trading at around 48x earnings, a hefty premium relative to the broader market (the S&P 500 trades at around 20x earnings, while the Nasdaq-100 is around 27x earnings). While Costco is a premium business, that's more than I'm willing to pay. I'd be more interested if shares fell closer to $825, or about 36x earnings.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Rollins (ROL +0.93%), the parent of Orkin, sells an essential service: pest control. It's an under-appreciated business model, as pest control is a route-based business where density, pricing power, and tuck-in deals compound returns, and demand holds up well when the economy softens.

    According to recent reports, the firm is currently battling an unexpected headwind. While its revenue rose 6.2% in the third quarter, organic growth was only 4.4%. Meanwhile, Rollins trimmed its full-year organic growth outlook to 4%-6% (from 7%-8%). The culprit: AI-driven changes in search that have disrupted how residential customers find pest control providers.

    Sources indicate that this headwind has weighed on the stock, which is down more than 40% from its recent peak. However, at nearly $38 per share, it's still rather expensive at over 30x earnings. After a growth downshift, I'd rather pay $30 to $33, or 24 to 27 times earnings.

    It has been revealed that cintas (CTAS +1.67%) helps millions of businesses get ready for their workday by renting uniforms and providing first-aid, safety, and fire-protection services on recurring routes, where each additional stop costs less to serve. That density, plus cross-selling services, has fueled steady growth.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    In a recent development, the firm reported record results in its fiscal 2027 first quarter, including record revenue (up 10.9% to $3 billion) and margins. Meanwhile, Cintas hiked its guidance, raising its adjusted earnings per share range to $5.45 to $5.54. Cintas also has a pending deal to acquire UniFirst, a transformational transaction that would enhance its capabilities and margins.

    The only thing not to like about Cintas is the valuation. At around $220, it trades at about 40x earnings. I'd prefer to pay closer to $185 a share, or less than 35x earnings.

    McKesson (MCK -1.97%) sits at the center of the pharmaceutical supply chain. It serves as the logistical and operational backbone of the U.S. healthcare system, including the distribution of pharmaceuticals and medical-surgical supplies to pharmacies and hospitals.

    In a recent development, revenue rose 8% in its fiscal 2027 second quarter to almost $111 billion, while its adjusted earnings per share jumped 18%. It raised its full-year earnings guidance range to $45.60-$46.40 per share, a 17% to 19% increase from last fiscal year.

    At its recent price of around $1,070, McKesson trades at about 23x earnings. I'd be more interested in paying less than 20x earnings for this healthcare logistics company, or less than $900 per share.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Roper (ROP -0.37%) is a diversified technology firm. It acquires software and technology-enabled businesses in specialized niche markets like legal, education, and construction. The company generates recurring revenue, which it routinely redeploys to acquire additional businesses. It deployed $436 million during the third quarter toward three bolt-on acquisitions.

    The manufacturer's revenue rose 8% in the third quarter (7% organically), while adjusted earnings per share grew 15%. Roper also increased its full-year guidance and has more than $6 billion of capacity to deploy into future acquisitions as opportunities arise.

    At nearly $460 a share, Roper trades at more than 20x earnings. Given the potential AI headwinds facing the software sector, I'd prefer to pay less than $425 per share, or around 19x earnings.

    These five businesses share an important trait: each has competitive strengths that could create shareholder value for many years. However, the price you pay for a great business is still important. That's why I'm making a list now, so that I'm ready to buy these excellent businesses if they fall to a more attractive valuation should the recent sell-off intensify.

    By Patrick Sanders – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:30AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Amazon ›.

    Industry observers note that anthropic (ANT -1.43%) started its life as a publicly traded company with a bang on Nov. 19. The artificial intelligence company behind Claude priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share, opened at $111.50, and finished its first day at $97.17.

    According to recent reports, anthropic instantly joined an exclusive club. With a valuation of $1.2 trillion (using only shares outstanding), it's one of only 15 companies with a market cap over $1 trillion as of this writing.

    But there's an even more exclusive grouping -- the Magnificent Seven, which are seven tech-centric stocks that have been responsible for a large part of the stock market's gains in recent quarters.

    Several members of the Magnificent Seven have substantial investments in Anthropic, and those lucrative business relationships could pay off for years.

    Amazon (AMZN +3.47%) and Alphabet (GOOGL +6.34%) (GOOG +5.88%) were early investors in Anthropic, and as Claude has grown, so have their stakes.

    According to Anthropic's prospectus, Amazon owns approximately 14.7% of Anthropic, and Alphabet holds another 13.7%. Based on its current valuation of $1.21 trillion, Amazon's stake is worth $177.87 billion, and Alphabet's is worth $165.77 billion.

    But it doesn't stop there. Anthropic also has business relationships with Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud for the computing power needed to train and operate Claude.

    Anthropic has committed to spending at least $110 billion with Amazon between May 2026 and April 2036, and at least $121.3 billion with Google, which also supplies its custom Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) for AI workloads.

    So, Amazon and Alphabet benefit in two ways -- their ownership stakes become more valuable as Anthropic grows, and their cloud businesses collect revenue directly from Anthropic.

    Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) and Microsoft (MSFT +1.65%) are also members of the Magnificent Seven. Both have smaller financial stakes in Anthropic and are also positioned to benefit from its growth.

    Industry observers note that nvidia agreed to purchase $10 billion of Anthropic shares through a private placement associated with the IPO. Microsoft committed another $1 billion.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia also supplies the graphics processing units (GPUs) used in AI computing. Anthropic's infrastructure strategy includes Nvidia GPUs alongside chips from Amazon, Google, and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD +6.85%).

    Microsoft also has cloud computing arrangements with Anthropic through its Microsoft Azure cloud, but its financial exposure is considerably smaller than that of Amazon or Alphabet.

    The relationships among major technology companies are complicated, particularly with regard to artificial intelligence. Companies such as Anthropic, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Nvidia are investors, suppliers, customers, and competitors -- seemingly all at the same time.

    Billions of dollars flow among these companies through investments, cloud computing contracts, and chip purchases. And while that creates opportunities for multiple companies to benefit from AI spending, it also raises questions about how much demand comes from companies financing their own customers.

NextEra Energy Resources focuses on contracted energy generation and battery storage, serving other utilities and commercial customers across North America through extensive long-term power sales agreements.

    It has been revealed that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue was nearly $28.8 billion, which is growth of roughly 9.6% over the previous period. This steady growth reflects the consistent demand for electricity in its Florida service area and the expansion of its renewable energy portfolio. Net income for the period reached approximately $11.6 billion, resulting in a net margin of roughly 40.4%, demonstrating the high profitability of its energy infrastructure operations.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Bloom Energy faces significant risks related to the emerging market for hydrogen and fuel cell power, which may not reach expected demand levels. The manufacturer deals with long sales and installation cycles, especially for its AI data center clients, and depends on fluctuating government tax incentives. It also faces intense competition and is currently involved in class action lawsuits concerning securities fraud and its sourcing of certain materials.

    In a recent development, nextEra Energy faces substantial regulatory risks as an electric utility, as state authorities can disallow the recovery of certain costs. Its Florida operations are vulnerable to severe weather events like hurricanes, while its nuclear facilities involve risks related to decommissioning and waste storage. The manufacturer is also navigating litigation related to political controversies and risks associated with major acquisitions, such as the planned purchase of Dominion Energy (D +0.77%).

    NextEra Energy is cheaper than Bloom Energy based on its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio and its price-to-sales (P/S) ratio.

    Both investments could fit together in a portfolio, but as individual stock picks, Bloom is better suited to those with a higher risk tolerance seeking stock price appreciation. It's rapidly increasing its revenue, jumping from $519 million in the third quarter of 2025 to $1.2 billion in the third quarter of 2026. Bloom's story is also becoming one of profitability, as it reported a net profit of $250.2 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to a net loss of $23 million in the prior-year period. While that's promising for Bloom's long-term outlook, the challenge will be that, if AI demand slows, it will be a difficult revenue gap to fill.

    In comparison, NextEra Energy is more about stability, operating Florida Power & Light. Shares are up only 4.6% this year, but the company also pays a dividend that yields nearly 3%, helping boost total returns. That said, it also has some interesting opportunities in nuclear energy and natural gas, and its potential acquisition of Dominion would give it a massive presence throughout Virginia, North Carolina, and South Carolina.

    Again, I still see room for both in a portfolio, so long as an investor knows the purpose each serves.

    The first of six Traits of a Rule Breaker Stock is: Top Dog and First-Mover in an Important, Emerging Industry.

    Many of the best stocks of every era lead a fresh industry that matters. Being first and biggest also tends to feed itself, because the leader usually finds it easier to attract top talent and raise money.

    CrowdStrike built its lead protecting computers and cloud systems. Its latest quarter showed that lead is still growing.     • Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
    • It has been revealed that the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    It has been revealed that the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo noted. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Industry observers note that securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and revealed the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo stated.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Patrick Sanders – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:42AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Alphabet ›.

    In a recent development, there's no question that Apple (AAPL +1.90%) and Microsoft (MSFT +1.65%) are two great tech stocks. I wouldn't argue with anyone who bought them. But my favorite “Magnificent Seven” stock all year has been Alphabet (GOOGL +6.34%) (GOOG +5.88%), and nothing that has happened so far in 2026 has changed my mind.

    Sources indicate that the biggest feather in Alphabet's cap remains its dominance in internet search. Google has 91% of the global search engine market share, which makes it an enormously profitable advertising platform.

    Industry observers note that google Search revenue was $63.3 billion in the third quarter, up 12% from a year earlier. And the Google services division, which includes Search, YouTube, and other businesses, brought in $96.3 billion in revenue — a massive revenue stream.

    It's hard to believe that the market once considered artificial intelligence, including AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude, a fundamental threat to Google's search business. But instead, Google has incorporated its Gemini AI assistant into its search engine, making it even better. It turned a potential threat into an advantage.

    Google Cloud doesn't bring in as much revenue as the tech giant's advertising engine, but it's catching up fast. Google Cloud revenue was $30.7 billion in the third quarter, up 103% from a year ago. Its operating income more than tripled to $11.1 billion, and its operating margin was an impressive 36.2%.

    And just as crucial, Google Cloud ended the quarter with a $561 billion backlog. Management expects more than 55% of that to convert into revenue within two years.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    Alphabet's cloud business is more than just providing computing power to its customers. Google also designs its own custom chips, which it calls Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). These specialized processors are narrowly tailored for AI workloads, but for those specific tasks, they can compete directly with GPUs designed by Nvidia (NVDA +31.48%) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD +6.85%)for cost-efficiency and power. The company said TPU system sales made a meaningful contribution to third-quarter growth.

    Anthropic's (ANT -1.43%) successful IPO on Nov. 19 gave Alphabet another reason to celebrate. According to Anthropic's prospectus, Google has a 13.7% stake in the market's newest trillion-dollar organization. And its relationship extends beyond the ownership stake. Anthropic has committed to spending at least $121.3 billion on Google’s cloud computing services through July 2033.

    Alphabet has a profitable advertising business, a rapidly expanding cloud operation, its own custom AI chips, and a valuable stake in one of the industry's most prominent AI companies. I liked Alphabet at the beginning of 2026 because it had multiple ways to win. Eleven months later, those opportunities look even better.

    • By The Rule Breakers Team – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:42AM EST.
    • Yesterday, Zoom Communications (ZM +5.87%) reported its fastest enterprise revenue growth in 13 quarters and declared its first-ever dividend.
    • For Team Rule Breakers, the report lands on two recommendations that haven't worked out, at least so far.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By The Rule Breakers Team – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:42AM EST.

    Yesterday, Zoom Communications (ZM +5.87%) reported its fastest enterprise revenue growth in 13 quarters and declared its first-ever dividend. The stock rose about 5% in regular trading.

    For Team Rule Breakers, the report lands on two recommendations that haven't worked out, at least so far.

    The sixth Habit of a Rule Breaker Investor is: Aim for 60% Accuracy.

    Recent findings suggest that A stock pick is accurate if it beats the S&P 500. No investor gets every call right, and trying for perfection can make people too cautious to own the stocks that win massive. The Rule Breaker approach aims to be right about six times in 10. A few big winners can then more than make up for the picks that lag.

    Industry observers note that team Rule Breakers recommended Zoom in Stock Advisor on March 19 and April 16, 2020, at $123.77 and $150.26. Those were the early weeks of the pandemic, when Zoom became a household name. Since then, the March recommendation is down about 30%, and the April one is down more than 40%. Both trail the S&P 500 by a wide margin.

    The business slowed far more than many investors expected. Revenue grew about 4% last fiscal year. Recommendations like these are part of aiming for 60%, and they're why the winners in a portfolio have to do the heavy lifting.

    On Nov. 10, Team Hidden Gems closed its three Zoom positions in Stock Advisor. It argued that AI agents could shrink Zoom's business, since Zoom charges mostly per person and fewer people may need to join meetings. It also noted that growth from existing customers had stalled, and that it had given the stock more than five years. Team Rule Breakers kept its two positions.

    Sources indicate that yesterday's report highlighted some progress on those points. Enterprise revenue rose 8.6% to $805.4 million. Existing enterprise customers are now spending about as much as a year ago, up from slightly less. Total revenue still grew only 4.9%, though, and online revenue slipped 0.6%.

    In a recent development, zoom holds about $7.3 billion in cash and marketable securities. It invested in Anthropic in early 2023, and that stake is now estimated at about $3.8 billion, roughly 15% of Zoom's market value. Anthropic only recently went public, so the stake's value could swing sharply. Zoom has also kept buying back stock, and its upcoming dividend pays $0.25 per share each quarter.

    Those strengths don't fix the main risk. If AI cuts the number of people who need a paid Zoom account, the core business could shrink even as the company invests in newer products like its AI customer-service agent.

    It has been revealed that aiming for 60% doesn't tell investors whether to sell any one loser. It asks them to judge the whole portfolio, where a handful of big winners usually decides the result. Team Hidden Gems decided Zoom's original thesis no longer fit, while Team Rule Breakers has kept its positions.

    Either choice can be reasonable within a diversified portfolio. What matters more is that no single holding grows large enough to sink the portfolio if it keeps lagging.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Bitcoin or Gold? Cathie Wood of Ark Invest Makes a Compelling Case for Buying Bitcoin.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (680 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, cathie Wood's investment thesis for buying Bitcoin (BTC -1.54%) instead of gold is an outlier, but it could prove prescient.
    • She expects Bitcoin to keep outperforming gold, and she also expects that what's good for one asset may not have much effect on the other.
    • According to recent reports, cathie Wood.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Alex Carchidi – Nov 24, 2026 at 6:45AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bitcoin ›.

    According to recent reports, cathie Wood's investment thesis for buying Bitcoin (BTC -1.54%) instead of gold is an outlier, but it could prove prescient. On Nov. 9, the Ark Invest chief executive officer remarked "gold is going down" and continued to argue that Bitcoin's correlation with gold has been minuscule since 2019.

    She expects Bitcoin to keep outperforming gold, and she also expects that what's good for one asset may not have much effect on the other. That's a bet on the ratio between their prices, so Bitcoin could still fall in dollar terms -- but is Wood's idea fundamentally sound?

    According to recent reports, cathie Wood. Image source: Getty Images.

    The correlation coefficient of two assets measures how closely their prices move together, from -1 (moving in opposite directions) to 1 (moving in lockstep). Bitcoin's correlation with SPDR Gold Shares, a popular gold exchange-traded fund (ETF), has averaged 0.13 during the past 10 years. Thus, the core of Wood's argument is grounded in fact.

    But take a look at this chart, which shows the fluctuation of the correlation over time:.

    Fundamental Chart data by YCharts.

    In a recent development, as you can see, there are many brief periods when gold and Bitcoin are highly correlated, and many when they're strongly negatively correlated. While it's true that the average of all these fluctuations is about 0.13, a very weak correlation, there actually aren't ever any periods longer than a few months within the last 10 years where that value is in force.

    CRYPTO · As of 7:01 AM ET 11/24/26.

    Industry observers note that in September, Wood said that Bitcoin was "both a risk-off and a risk-on asset," meaning that (in theory) it can rally when investors are seeking safety and when they're seeking growth. In practice, Bitcoin has mostly traded like a risk-on asset, often falling in market sell-offs, sometimes right alongside gold. Gold, she told Fox Business in December 2025, is "more of a risk-off asset," which is consistent with what most investors believe about it and with its historical performance.

    Wood also argues that Bitcoin's supply makes it a superior store of value to gold over the long run. Bitcoin's circulating supply expands by about 0.8% annually, versus about 1.8% for gold, whose miners can dig more when prices rise. Plus, Bitcoin's supply is limited to 21 million bitcoins of which more than 20 million are already in circulation. Gold has no fixed cap, and its output rises with price.

    During the past 10 years, Bitcoin's annualized volatility (how widely its price swings in a year) was 56.7%, whereas the gold ETF's volatility was just 16%. Bitcoin's worst drops have topped 80% several times, while the gold ETF's worst-ever loss was 45.6%.

    NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    It has been revealed that an asset that can lose most of its value can't reliably guard your purchasing power. Gold's adoption is also mature after centuries in central bank vaults and institutional portfolios, while Bitcoin's 17-year-old adoption story is still relatively latest, leaving more room for new buyers.

    Industry observers note that wood's supply argument is the compelling part of her case, since Bitcoin's issuance is fixed and slowing while gold's rises with its price. Even so, I'm not convinced Bitcoin will keep outrunning gold the way Wood expects, and I don't find her correlation argument very persuasive. Still, most portfolios can stand to hold both some gold and some Bitcoin, and there isn't much point in committing to buy only one or the other.

    #165230. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (740 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (740 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the organization's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company.
    • Recent findings suggest that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the organization's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously announced commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate latest multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    According to recent reports, tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    Industry observers note that on Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    It's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The company had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    It has been revealed that coreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, remarked CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he mentioned in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any substantial changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real matter is just how much money the tech giant will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    "Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he stated. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    Billionaire Philippe Laffont of Coatue Management Sent AMD Shares Packing and Loaded Up on This Hot AI IPO Instead

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.
    • Although earnings season and Fed meetings tend to hog all the headlines, investors can learn a lot during Form 13F filing season.
    • Sources indicate that billionaire Philippe Laffont of Coatue Management is easily one of the most successful and closely watched fund managers on Wall Street -- and he was a busy bee during the third quarter.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sean Williams – Nov 24, 2026 at 7:06AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.

    Although earnings season and Fed meetings tend to hog all the headlines, investors can learn a lot during Form 13F filing season. A 13F allows investors to track which stocks Wall Street's savviest money managers, with at least $100 million in assets under management, purchased and sold in the latest quarter.

    Sources indicate that billionaire Philippe Laffont of Coatue Management is easily one of the most successful and closely watched fund managers on Wall Street -- and he was a busy bee during the third quarter. According to Coatue's 13F, Laffont sent shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD +6.85%) packing, while at the same time loading up on shares of one of Wall Street's hottest artificial intelligence (AI) initial public offerings (IPOs), SK Hynix (SKHY +20.00%).

    In a recent development, among Wall Street's billionaire investors, few have embraced the AI revolution quite like Laffont. As recently as mid-2023, his fund held approximately 14 million shares of AMD. By the end of 2025, all 14 million shares were given the heave-ho.

    Laffont bought back 95,987 shares in the second quarter of 2026, only to turn around and dump every last share the very next quarter.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/23/26.

    In a recent development, profit-taking is the most logical reason Coatue's billionaire boss bid adieu to AMD. Between April and July, shares of the company soared from around $200 to more than $500. Coatue's average hold time is around three years, signaling a willingness by its chief investor to ring the register when given the opportunity.

    However, profit-taking may not be the only reason AMD was jettisoned. While Laffont isn't exactly a value investor, AMD's estimated price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio for 2026 and 2027 was approaching 80 and 40, respectively, toward the end of September. With AMD holding such a small share of the AI-accelerating graphics processing unit (GPU) market, Laffont may have viewed other AI stocks as more intriguing.

    Although everyone's talking about Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +4.35%) and Anthropic (ANT -1.43%) breaking the IPO record books, they're overlooking SK Hynix, which also debuted in the U.S. in July as a trillion-dollar manufacturer. Laffont purchased 9,498,922 shares, worth almost $1.75 billion at the end of the third quarter.

    Laffont's attraction to SK Hynix likely has to do with its world-leading position as a supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM). HBM is stacked with GPUs to facilitate ultra-fast transfer speeds in enterprise data centers. Not only is SK Hynix benefiting from strong demand for HBM, but persistent supply shortages are also pushing its pricing power into the stratosphere.

    One of the wildest things about AI memory shortage is that regular DRAM now costs more per GB than HBM which tells you just how much demand is reshaping the market.And AI needs far more than just HBM so here's how the six layers of memory and storage break down: • SRAM… pic.twitter.com/2c45sjiG9P.

    Industry observers note that SK Hynix foresees memory shortages potentially lasting through 2030. According to a late-October revision, the company has already secured purchase agreements for more than half of its production for 2027 and 2028. Wall Street (and billionaire investor Philippe Laffont) appreciates cash-flow predictability.

    But SK Hynix isn't necessarily a slam-dunk investment. While its purchase agreements can temporarily buoy its pricing power, history shows that memory is cyclical and highly commoditized, and strong pricing power is rarely sustainable. If the AI bubble bursts, as history suggests will happen sooner rather than later, SK Hynix's pricing power could take a direct hit.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hungary manager Marco Rossi has defended his usage of Dominik Szoboszlai during this international window.
    • The Liverpool midfielder sprained his knee during the Reds’ 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace the weekend before last and admitted that he nearly pulled out of his country’s win over Georgia six days later.
    • His choice to represent his nation was condemned by some reporters back on Merseyside, amid fears of aggravating the injury and compromising his involvement for his club over the coming weeks as the fixtures come thick and fast for Andoni Iraola’s side.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hungary manager Marco Rossi has defended his usage of Dominik Szoboszlai during this international window.

    The Liverpool midfielder sprained his knee during the Reds’ 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace the weekend before last and admitted that he nearly pulled out of his country’s win over Georgia six days later.

    His choice to represent his nation was condemned by some reporters back on Merseyside, amid fears of aggravating the injury and compromising his involvement for his club over the coming weeks as the fixtures come thick and fast for Andoni Iraola’s side.

    Rossi was defiant when quizzed about Szoboszlai ahead of Hungary’s match against Northern Ireland on Tuesday night.

    He told reporters (via Origo Sport): “Did you see any problems with Dominik in the Georgia game? Because I didn’t see any. He played like he usually does, so there are no problems from our side. He states he’s ready, he’s available, so he’ll play.”.

    The Hungary boss was true to his word, as the Liverpool star played the entirety of the Northern Ireland game, thankfully seeming to come through it without any adverse effects.

    Industry observers note that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    We can understand Szoboszlai wanting to represent his country, especially in his role as captain, but those who pay his wages at Anfield mightn’t have been overly impressed with his decision to play on despite knowing prior to the Georgia match that he wasn’t operating at 100%.

    That Liverpool don’t play until Sunday at 4:30pm gives the 26-year-old that bit of additional time to manage his fitness carefully so that he’s in prime condition for the game against Manchester United.

    Whether or not the midfielder will start that match is debatable. The in-form Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz will likely have two of the three midfield berths nailed down, and the excellent displays of Trey Nyoni have made it difficult to omit him from the XI.

    Also, if Iraola feels that Szoboszlai isn’t fully fit by Sunday, he probably won’t take the risk of throwing our number 8 back into the starting line-up, instead keeping him in reserve should he be needed off the bench.

    Hopefully the influential Hungarian won’t suffer any further complications over the next four days, and everyone associated with Liverpool will surely be glad that the international window is out of the way, with the next one not upon us until late March 2027.

    #165211. Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (582 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (582 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).
    • Industry observers note that is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?
    • It has been revealed that first, let's remember how we got here.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

    Industry observers note that is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

    It has been revealed that first, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout rapidly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

    The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

    It has been revealed that zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three important forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

    This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

    For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

    Recent findings suggest that the following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

    Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

    The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

    The major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

    That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

    One key clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

    Any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

    We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

    The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

    From here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see new highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

    #165192. A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (625 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct.
    • However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive.
    • Recent findings suggest that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession initiative, makes it worse.

    However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a big haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the manufacturer's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

    Recent findings suggest that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options. Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

    In a recent development, this prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

    It has been revealed that this lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

    By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

    #165168. Breaking: Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1101 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1101 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.
    • Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.
    • The much more widely held B shares closed at newly introduced highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

    Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

    The much more widely held B shares closed at newly introduced highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

    The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

    Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

    Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

    After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

    They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

    Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

    We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the firm's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

    It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

    As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

    On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

    Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

    If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

    The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the firm as "banks, insurance, and finance.".

    The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

    Barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks new CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

    In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to swiftly disclose any sales.

    Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

    That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

    The case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

    Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

    Industry observers note that in the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

    All those numbers exclude the firm's buybacks of its own stock.

    In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway says it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

    Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

    It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

    In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

    Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

    Some links may require a subscription:.

    Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most important ideas.

    WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

    You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

    Two of the — well, all of the important ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

    One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

    According to recent reports, and the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

    And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that says it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds.".

    Berkshire market capitalization: $1,259,897,054,755.

    Berkshire Cash as of Sept 30: $377.4 billion (Up 3.3% from June 30).

    Excluding Rail Cash and Subtracting T-Bills Payable: $352.3 billion (Down 1.9% from June 30).

    Berkshire repurchased $9.6 billion of its shares in Q3 2026.

    Berkshire's top holdings of disclosed publicly traded stocks in the U.S. and Japan, by market value, based on the latest closing prices.

    Holdings are as of June 30, 2026, as reported in Berkshire Hathaway's 13F filing on August 14, 2026, except for:.
