Of the 42,300 contracts traded by midday, 41,800 were calls, with just 141 puts likely opened by buyers.

    It has been revealed that just shy of $5.5 million in options premium on DXYZ traded on Monday, with almost all of it tied to calls, but just marginally more spent buying than selling calls, according to SpotGamma. The highest-volume contract is at the moment the 30-strike call expiring Friday, a 90-cent contract that needs the fund to rally 19% into the weekend to pay off.Traders may want to be wary of how the fund traded around the SpaceX IPO: DXYZ surged almost 150% in May before unwinding all the gains in the weeks ahead of SpaceX's debut. Since then, the fund has barely moved, trading around $26.There are other bullish signs surrounding Anthropic's IPO in the derivatives markets. Current prices for perpetual futures on the blockchain exchange Hyperliquid are implying an opening price of $98, a massive pop from the $70-$78 price range quoted in the firm's amended S1 filing. The AI giant is expected to price Wednesday evening and begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.

    #165133. Latest manager bounce? How Mauricio Pochettino fared in his first match in charge of previous clubs

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (687 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Empireofthekop ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest manager bounce? How Mauricio Pochettino fared in his first match in charge of previous clubs

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (687 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Empireofthekop

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Liverpool will be wary of the threat of ‘latest manager bounce’ on Sunday when they face a Manchester United team now under the management of Mauricio Pochettino.
    • Having sacked Michael Carrick last Thursday, the Red Devils moved swiftly to appoint the Argentine as his successor, with their upcoming head coach signing off from a similar role with the United States with a 2-0 win over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League.
    • The Old Trafford outfit enjoyed an immediate upsurge in form when their former midfielder replaced Ruben Amorim back in January, but how has the fresh man in charge fared in his first game at his five previous spells as a club boss?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Liverpool will be wary of the threat of ‘latest manager bounce’ on Sunday when they face a Manchester United team now under the management of Mauricio Pochettino.

    Having sacked Michael Carrick last Thursday, the Red Devils moved swiftly to appoint the Argentine as his successor, with their upcoming head coach signing off from a similar role with the United States with a 2-0 win over Haiti in the CONCACAF Nations League.

    The Old Trafford outfit enjoyed an immediate upsurge in form when their former midfielder replaced Ruben Amorim back in January, but how has the fresh man in charge fared in his first game at his five previous spells as a club boss?

    Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

    Espanyol were in the LaLiga relegation zone when Pochettino took charge almost 18 years ago, and his first task seemed a daunting one against city rivals Barcelona, who’d end the season as treble winners under Pep Guardiola.

    The Argentine had only two training sessions to implement his methods before the Copa Del Rey derby fixture, but his new team claimed an impressive share of the spoils on home turf before narrowly losing the second leg 3-2 at Camp Nou. A few weeks later, he masterminded a shock league victory at the home of their arch-rivals.

    The Saints’ decision to axe the popular Nigel Adkins mid-season was met with shock throughout English football, with the south coast club well on their way to staying up in their first season back in the Premier League after a seven-year absence.

    He again drew 0-0 in his first game of a managerial spell, with Southampton putting in a battling performance against an Everton side who, at the time, were outside contenders for Champions League qualification under David Moyes.

    (Photo by Ian Walton/Getty Images).

    This was Pochettino’s first time having a full summer to prepare for a managerial job rather than coming in mid-season, earning the Spurs gig off the back of his fine work at Southampton.

    The north Londoners survived a red card and a missed Mark Noble penalty before snatching all three points in stoppage time courtesy of an Eric Dier goal on what was also his first outing with Tottenham, who left the Boleyn Ground with a sweet win over their capital rivals.

    It was back to mid-season appointments for Pochettino six-and-a-half years later as he filled the vacancy left by Thomas Tuchel’s departure for Chelsea.

    Recent findings suggest that he maintained his record of never losing his first game in charge of a club, but in truth this was two points dropped for PSG, who at the time were three points adrift of surprise Ligue 1 leaders Lyon. They also had to come from behind against an in-form Les Verts side.

    Sunday won’t be the first time that Liverpool provide the opposition for Pochettino in his first game in charge – the Reds also had that role when the Argentine began his reign as Chelsea boss three years ago.

    Once again he’d end with a draw, as an entertaining clash on the opening weekend of the Premier League season saw Luis Diaz’s opener for the visitors cancelled out by Axel Disasi as each team had a further goal disallowed.

    Four draws and a win for Pochettino from his managerial debuts at his previous clubs – it’s a respectable record, but not an overly intimidating one.

    According to recent reports, it feels more pertinent to look at his first results when taking charge mid-season, just as he’s doing now with Man United. All three of those games were drawn, and another such result on Sunday would be regarded as a decent start for him.

    It’d also represent disappointment for Liverpool, who are without an Anfield win over their arch-rivals in three attempts since the famous 7-0 romp in March 2023.

    #165117. Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (516 w)

    Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (516 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
    • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
    • Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting massive moves.

    With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

    Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the company that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

    "Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, mentioned in a text ahead of the organization's after-market report on Tuesday.

    Since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is right now 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

    The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

    Sources indicate that one catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

    Industry observers note that with bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

    By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

    Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

    #165112. Commanders QB Jayden Daniels hits a pair of big passes to set up game-winning field goal to beat Bengals

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1747 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Commanders QB Jayden Daniels hits a pair of big passes to set up game-winning field goal to beat Bengals

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1747 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, it looked like Joe Burrow might have added to his MVP résumé by leading a game-winning drive.
    • After the Cincinnati Bengals kicked a field goal with 46 seconds left to take a 20-19 lead, Daniels hit two huge passes downfield to get the Washington Commanders in range for a short field goal and the win.
    • Industry observers note that the Bengals had a shot to end the game but couldn't run more time off the clock after getting in field-goal range.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, it looked like Joe Burrow might have added to his MVP résumé by leading a game-winning drive. But Jayden Daniels got the last word.

    After the Cincinnati Bengals kicked a field goal with 46 seconds left to take a 20-19 lead, Daniels hit two huge passes downfield to get the Washington Commanders in range for a short field goal and the win. Drew Stevens made the kick and Washington escaped with a 22-20 win.

    Industry observers note that the Bengals had a shot to end the game but couldn't run more time off the clock after getting in field-goal range. That allowed Daniels a shot. He hit rookie Antonio Williams for 22 yards and then 42 yards to set up the win on Stevens' 26-yard field goal.

    Burrow had taken over as the MVP favorite before Monday night's game. But Daniels has had moments as a special quarterback, too, and he and Williams had a magical couple of plays to pull out a dramatic win.

    It has been revealed that the game didn't start with the Bengals tearing up a defense, as has been the case in recent weeks. The game was scoreless after the first quarter, mostly due to rain. That affected both offenses, though the weather cleared up and both teams started to move the ball better.

    The Bengals took a 10-0 lead on a great catch in the end zone by Tee Higgins for a 31-yard score.

    Industry observers note that the Commanders had their protection issues in the first half, most notably blocking Boye Mafe who had three sacks before halftime. But a long drive near the end of the first half resulted in a Jacory Croskey-Merritt touchdown, and early in the first half a 47-yard run by Daniels set up a game-tying field goal.

    The Bengals had been one of the hottest offenses in the NFL but the Commanders did a good job keeping pressure on Burrow and containing him, with an assist from the weather early in the game.

    In a recent development, the Bengals got a touchdown to take the lead in the third quarter, as Burrow hit rookie Colbie Young for a 4-yard score after the QB was chased out of the pocket. But the Bengals couldn't do much else for most of the second half.

    Sources indicate that part of the problem is they can't run the ball, and have given up trying. The Commanders had a good plan against a pass-heavy offense and the Bengals didn't have a counter-punch. That could end up being a problem for Cincinnati in the playoffs.

    Industry observers note that the Commanders weren't doing much themselves on offense, but had a couple field goals to keep them in the game. Then came a long drive at the right time. Highlighted by Stefon Diggs' 29-yard catch on second-and-20, the Commanders chewed up a lot of clock and took a lead. The Commanders had a big decision, whether to go for it on fourth-and-1 with less than two minutes left. Washington kicked the field goal for the 19-17 lead, but that left Burrow 2:26 to get in field-goal range and retake the lead.

    In a recent development, burrow got the drive going with a 12-yard pass to Higgins, and then he hit tight end Mike Gesicki for 32 yards. That put the Bengals in field-goal range and led to the Commanders starting to call their timeouts. There was almost a game-ending mistake from Burrow, but rookie linebacker Sonny Styles had a pass go off his hands and it was incomplete rather than an interception. Then Burrow took a sack, which was a loss of eight yards and made the field goal harder. McPherson came on for a 56-yard attempt and he nailed it. At that point it seemed like Cincinnati would escape.

    Industry observers note that daniels had 46 seconds to answer. And he did, going to the middle of the field twice for Williams for major gains. Williams told ESPN afterward that the Commanders ran the same play for both catches.

    Industry observers note that the win helped the Commanders improve to 4-5-1. Washington still has a ways to go to get back in the NFC East race, but Daniels will do his best to keep the Commanders in it.

    Antonio Williams finished the night with 9 catches for 122 yards, including 64 on Washington's game-winning drive.

    Drew Stevens connected on all five of his field-goal attempts, including a walk-off winner.

    Recent findings suggest that and Jayden Daniels delivered when it mattered most. He finished the night completing 23 of 35 passes for 289 yards while adding 55 yards on the ground, including a 47-yard run that set up a Washington score.

    What way to cap Week 11 with one of the unlikeliest wins of the season.

    Jayden Daniels found Antonio Williams for a 22-yard gain and then a 44-yard gain to get the Commanders in field goal territory despite starting the possession with no timeouts and 46 seconds left on the clock.

    Drew Stevens delivered with a walk-off field goal from 26 yards out to cap a stunning, 22-20 come-from-behind Commanders win.

    Joe Burrow took a sack to push a field-goal attempt back to 56 yards, but Evan McPherson delivered.

    The Bengals kicker was pure from long distance, and the Bengals are back on top with a 20-19 lead. Washington has 46 seconds to answer.

    The Bengals have moved the ball into field-goal range, and the Commanders just missed a golden opportunity at an interception. The ball bounced off of Sonny Style's fingertips then through the hands of Rasul Douglas, who had a play on the ball.

    Washington had a decision with fourth-and-less-than-yard in field-goal territory.

    Dan Quinn decided to take the points after Stefon Diggs came up just short of a first down from the Cincinnati 24-yard line, and Drew Stevens delivered with a 41-yard field goal.

    According to recent reports, the score gives the commanders a 19-17 lead, but Joe Burrow and the Bengals have the ball and 2:26 remaining on the clock in need of just a field goal to re-take the lead. A first down would have given the Commanders a chance to burn clock and score a touchdown.

    Stefon Diggs, who's been animated with his frustration all night, just got the Commanders over midfield on a significant pass play with a chance to take a fourth-quarter lead.

    The Commanders should keep throwing it to Chig Okonkwo.

    Sources indicate that cincinnati's offense is suddenly toothless again. The Bengals punted after five plays, and the Commanders have the ball back with 8:30 remaining and a 17-16 deficit.

    If they Commanders lose, they're gonna look back on some missed opportunities.

    Jayden Daniels scrambled to buy time on third-and-goal, but his pass to Stefon Diggs in the end zone bounced short off the turf.

    Drew Stevens instead connected from 25 yards to cap a third consecutive Washington possesion with a field goal, and Cincinnati remains in front, 17-16.

    Here's Joe Buck with why the lights went out in Landover:.

    "The official word is the lighting vendor never disabled the regularly scheduled maintenance for 10 p.m. It's a weekday thing, and they forgot that it was a Monday night game.".

    Joe Burrow had Ja'Marr Chase on a deep post route, and he just missed.

    It has been revealed that chase beat double coverage and had a chance for a massive gain, but the ball was just out of his grasp. The result is a 3-and-out punt for the Bengals and a chance for Washington to take the lead with a 17-13 deficit.

    Barring the end of the half, that's now five consecutive possessions with a score.

    The Commanders have three of them, but two are field goals, including Drew Stevens' 40-yard effort just now after Washington stalled out on third-and-4.

    The Bengals have countered with consecutive touchdown drives and have a 17-13 lead with 2:36 remaining in the third quarter as a result.

    Joe Burrow escaped pressure, scrambled and kept a play alive to find rookie receiver Colbie Young in the end zone for Young's first career touchdown.

    The 4-yard scored capped a quick-strike 66-yard drive that took just eight plays, and the Bengals offense is humming after a slow start.

    It has been revealed that OK, that didn't take long. The stadium lights were back in playing condition in just a few minutes.

    Washington failed to convert on fourth-and-14 on the first play back. Drew Stevens then converted on a field goal attempt from 37 yards, and the game is tied at 10-10 after the first possession of the second half.

    Here's the moment the lights went out.

    Industry observers note that this happened before the stadium went dark. Jayden Daniels set the Commanders up in the red zone with a 47-yard gain on a designed run. It's the longest run of Washington's season.

    Seriously, the lights went out with the Commanders in the red zone on third-and-14.

    Industry observers note that TV screens went completely dark before ambient lighting started coming back on. But it could be a while before they're back in playing condition.

    Sources indicate that the second half is underway. The Commanders have the ball and a chance to tie or take the lead, facing a 10-7 deficit.

    Both offenses got going late in the first half after slow starts on a wet field in Landover.

    Before a pair of late scores, both defenses were in control with pressure on Joe Burrow and Jayden Daniels.

    CommandersJayden Daniels: 8 of 11, 85 yards, 0 TDs or turnovers; 3 carries, 7 yardsChig Okonkwo: 1 catch, 32 yardsJacory Croskey-Merritt: 5 carries, 22 yards, 1 TD.

    Team statsBengals sacks: 3; all by Boye MafeCommanders sacks: 2; 1.5 by Tim Settle.

    Bengals total yards: 188 on 5.2 yards per playCommanders total yards: 107 on 4.5 yards per play.

    Bengals turnovers: 0Commanders turnovers: 0.

    After a slow start for both offenses, each team found the end zone at the end of the second quarter. The Bengals take a 10-7 lead into the halftime break, but the Commanders will start the second half with the ball.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the company "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    It has been revealed that the report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the tech giant kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also remarked that fresh export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    The allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    According to recent reports, "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson said in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    It has been revealed that lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the firm's recent earnings call that China is an "important" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

    #165099. ‘This establishes a bottom’: Jensen Huang’s return seen as likely to stop market sell-off, for now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (778 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    ‘This establishes a bottom’: Jensen Huang’s return seen as likely to stop market sell-off, for now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (778 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the major averages of U.S.
    • Industry observers note that the relief rally came after the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended Friday's session in correction territory.
    • According to recent reports, that sell-off may be over — at least temporarily — according to Wall Street experts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the major averages of U.S. equities surged on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, giving investors some hope that the relentless selling pressure seen last week may subside — at least temporarily.

    Industry observers note that the relief rally came after the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended Friday's session in correction territory. The S&P alone tumbled more than 9% after Huang's departure from the chipmaker was initially revealed on Nov. 12 through Friday.

    According to recent reports, that sell-off may be over — at least temporarily — according to Wall Street experts. But key questions linger around Nvidia and the artificial intelligence trade that has carried the bull market.

    "I think the AI trade is back on," noted Mark Gibbens, founder of Gibbens Capital Management. "I certainly believe this establishes a bottom and a floor in the AI trade and the recent market weakness.".

    It has been revealed that he added that the news likely doesn't alleviate all concerns that have driven recent declines, including worries about data center approvals after the midterms and fears that the capital expenditures cycle may have peaked. But Gibbens thinks the "keystone" role that Nvidia plays in both financing the AI buildout and the technology's supply chain means a more stable picture of the chipmaker creates a brighter view of the overall market than before.

    An encouraging sign that the correction may be over came even before Nvidia's Monday announcement, according to Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth Management. He noted Friday's selling, which was indiscriminate and affected sectors beyond just AI-exposed companies, indicated a bottom may have been building.

    "Sometimes you just hit that crescendo where you know the market gets oversold, and I would argue that we'd be higher today, even without the Nvidia news," he mentioned. Indeed, futures tied to the major stock indexes were broadly higher on Sunday night, before any news regarding Huang's return. "So I think that sort of signals we've likely found a place where we priced in, at least the near term, as much of the bad news that was giving markets jitters over the course of the last several weeks.".

    According to recent reports, strengthening the case for a bottom was that the technology sector's forward earnings valuation was cheaper than that of consumer staples, Hogan remarked. The S&P 500 consumer staples sector trades at a 20.5 multiple, per FactSet. Tech, meanwhile, trades at 16.3 times forward earnings. Hogan said that discrepancy doesn't square with the earnings outlook for the former sector.

    Industry observers note that jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets, said Huang's return created a relief rally for a market that was oversold. But he's not sure the headline alone can get the market out of its funk.

    "I think the rally will probably fizzle out because now people will pull back and still have the same questions we had before he was replaced," Woods said. Those questions will likely play out in congressional hearings, he speculated. "The market needed this jolt to get us back on our feet, but it is still a counter trend rally in an otherwise near-term downtrend.".

    Woods, though, stated that the lows for the year are likely in, thanks to Friday's wash-out that spread to all sectors beyond those dependent on Nvidia's role in AI.

    According to recent reports, while investors celebrated Huang's return, the sell-off that accelerated after his departure started before worries about his position even began. That stemmed from concerns about financing the buildout, data center approvals after Democratic wins in the midterm elections and worries that hyperscaler capex may have already peaked or is about to.

    That's why Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at One Point BFG Wealth Partners, is still nervous about the "picks and shovels" companies involved in the AI trade, a group he indicates includes Nvidia.

    Sources indicate that "We should enjoy this rally, and maybe it lasts a bit, but I think that picks and shovels trade is going to be solely dependent on what that rate of capex spend is going to be," he noted. "That, at the end of the day, is the story that those companies are going to have to deal with outside of bounces like we're seeing now.".

    Traders at Goldman Sachs put it more succinctly.

    Recent findings suggest that "Not sure yet whether good or bad that the fate of the market is almost equal to the fate of one person. But hey ... We are not picky here," they noted.

    — CNBC's Michelle Fox and Deena Zaidi contributed reporting.

    #165095. Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO. Stock skyrockets 31%

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1017 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO. Stock skyrockets 31%

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1017 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries.
    • The board of directors mentioned it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him.
    • President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries.

    The board of directors mentioned it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. The board added that it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

    President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard.".

    Huang resigned from his role as chief executive earlier this month after a series of shocking reports about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The New York Times reported on Sunday that the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security during at least part of the time that she was engaging in a relationship with Huang.

    Shares of Nvidia closed up 31% following Huang's reinstatement. The stock had shed nearly 33% from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on Nov. 8. The stock closed at $186.64 on Nov.6.

    "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a newly introduced industrial revolution," Huang stated in a statement. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.".

    Senior government officials briefed Nvidia's board late last week and communicated that no national security laws were violated, according to sources familiar with the discussion who asked to remain anonymous because they were not authorized to speak publicly. That upgrade prompted the board to reach out to Huang, the people noted.

    Industry observers note that huang and the board held their first conversations since his ouster on Saturday, and the group determined he would return as CEO during a second meeting on Sunday, the people stated. Nvidia's cratering stock price played a role in accelerating those conversations.

    Recent findings suggest that trump celebrated Huang's return to Nvidia on Monday, writing in a post on his social media site that the board made "the correct and proper decision" to reinstate him. Trump stated the U.S. needs Huang's leadership to "ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Organization, but the American Economy.".

    He reiterated that the U.S. government has "no reason to believe" Huang's return poses a risk to national security, and that it "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    "On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," Trump wrote.

    Several tech industry leaders, including Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX, Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer at Atreides Management, and Brad Gerstner, Altimeter Capital CEO, had been actively lobbying for Huang's return. Musk wrote in a post on X on Monday that the board's "mistake has been corrected.".

    Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.

    For weeks following Huang's ouster, the firm's board maintained that it was not considering Huang's reinstatement. It appointed Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer, as the chipmaker's interim CEO, who reiterated that position in an interview with CNBC following Huang's exit. Kress will continue to serve as Nvidia's CFO, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

    Sources indicate that nvidia's board formed an independent committee and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation into Huang and whether organization secrets or national security were compromised. The board stated Monday that "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion" and that Huang is "committed to cooperating with it.".

    According to recent reports, "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair, Harvey Jones, mentioned in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company.".

    Even with Huang back at the helm, Nvidia is facing increased scrutiny over its chip sales in Southeast Asia and China.

    According to recent reports, lawmakers have been preparing for investigations into how Huang's affair with the alleged spy may have damaged U.S. AI dominance, influenced his positions on export controls, and impacted his close relationships with Trump and his Cabinet. Huang has been one of the loudest voices opposing strict export controls on advanced chips.

    "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the manufacturer's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., remarked in a statement Monday.

    According to recent reports, huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, is scheduled to appear before the panels on Dec. 2. Those dates were set before Huang's return, and John Fisher, who represents Huang, did not comment on whether there are any changes in his intends to testify.

    Recent findings suggest that senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C., noted Monday that Huang will publicly testify on Dec. 3 as the sole witness during a hearing titled, "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls.".

    Sources indicate that "Americans deserve answers about what NVIDIA and the Trump administration knew, when they knew it, and whether sufficient steps were taken to prevent sensitive technology from falling into the wrong hands," Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., a member of the Banking Committee, wrote in a post on X on Monday.

    According to recent reports, trapped shareholders now face a classic post-crash hurdle: heavy overhead supply. Investors who bought near prior peaks often use sharp rebounds to exit at breakeven, creating stubborn technical resistance between $175 and $210 — especially with congressional testimony and export scrutiny still lingering.

    Rather than waiting passively for a full V-shaped surge to all-time highs, underwater holders can deploy a stock repair strategy geared toward a partial recovery.

    #165090. Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (755 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (755 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a big win for the organization and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    Industry observers note that some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    Industry observers note that adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and mentioned it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the big indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    In a recent development, "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he noted.

    Part of the challenge, Niles noted, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    Industry observers note that "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," remarked JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he stated, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    In a recent development, anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan said. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the firm in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    Industry observers note that "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he remarked. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    Recent findings suggest that one bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (706 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    CrowdStrike CEO defends Zscaler acquisition, calls it a 'winning combination'

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (706 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz on Monday defended the cybersecurity organization's planned acquisition of Zscaler, arguing the deal will strengthen its security capabilities and create significant growth opportunities despite a sharp sell-off in its shares.
    • "When you look at the tailwinds from these agentic attacks and you listen to customers, they're looking for a complete solution and a platform that delivers not only all of the capabilities we have, but also has network visibility, protection, and control, and zero trust from a network perspective," Kurtz told CNBC's Jim Cramer on "Mad Money." "This is why we acquired Zscaler today.
    • Shares of CrowdStrike fell roughly 9% Monday after the company announced it would acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at roughly $44 billion, raising investor concerns about dilution.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz on Monday defended the cybersecurity organization's planned acquisition of Zscaler, arguing the deal will strengthen its security capabilities and create significant growth opportunities despite a sharp sell-off in its shares.

    "When you look at the tailwinds from these agentic attacks and you listen to customers, they're looking for a complete solution and a platform that delivers not only all of the capabilities we have, but also has network visibility, protection, and control, and zero trust from a network perspective," Kurtz told CNBC's Jim Cramer on "Mad Money." "This is why we acquired Zscaler today. The technology, the team, and we think it's a winning combination putting it together with the CrowdStrike platform.".

    Shares of CrowdStrike fell roughly 9% Monday after the company announced it would acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at roughly $44 billion, raising investor concerns about dilution. The deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028. Zscaler shares rose more than 17%.

    The acquisition overshadowed CrowdStrike's better-than-expected quarterly results released Monday morning. The organization had been scheduled to report earnings on Dec. 1, but moved up the release date to coincide with the Zscaler announcement.

    Recent findings suggest that the acquisition fills a key gap in CrowdStrike's cybersecurity platform. While its Falcon platform protects devices and cloud systems, Zscaler adds security across the networks connecting them. Kurtz mentioned the deal expands CrowdStrike's addressable market by roughly $185 billion.

    CrowdStrike's largest acquisition to date comes amid a wave of consolidation in the cybersecurity industry as companies ramp up defenses against increasingly sophisticated AI-powered attacks. Recent high-profile hacks and technology outages have heightened concerns about vulnerabilities in corporate systems. CrowdStrike has been a major beneficiary of skyrocketing demand for AI security, with shares having soared about 96% this year entering Monday's session. For its part, Zscaler's stock ended last week down 13% year to date. As of Friday's close, the companies had a combined market value of more than $265 billion, trailing industry leader Palo Alto Networks at $282 billion.

    In a recent development, kurtz also highlighted the potential to sell more products across the combined customer base. He mentioned the companies share only about 2,000 accounts, leaving roughly 8,000 Zscaler customers that do not right now use CrowdStrike.

    Sources indicate that the companies are "very complementary overall," Kurtz noted. "There's very little overlap.".

    He emphasized that the announcement generated an overwhelmingly positive response from customers.

    Sources indicate that "Most important, customers demanded it. They loved it, and I can tell you, my phone blew up after the acquisition," Kurtz noted. "There's so many customers that love both us and Zscaler, and they're excited to see the acquisition news today.".

    To be sure, the all-stock deal has raised concerns about dilution, since CrowdStrike will issue new shares to pay for the acquisition, reducing existing shareholders' ownership stakes.

    Kurtz pushed back on those concerns, arguing that the combination will deliver immediate financial benefits. "On a free cash flow per share basis, it's immediately accretive right after close," he said. "With just modest synergies, you're going to have revenue, operating margin, and free cash flow margin accretion.".

    It has been revealed that he also downplayed integration risks, pointing to the companies' longstanding technology partnership. That relationship dates back to at least 2019, and the firms unveiled an expanded partnership in August 2025. "Zscaler is our No. 1 technology partner," Kurtz mentioned.

    In a separate "Mad Money" interview, Zscaler CEO and Founder Jay Chaudhry emphasized that combining the companies' platforms will better position them to combat a upcoming generation of AI-powered cyberattacks.

    "I think there's some areas where, by bringing the platforms together, we can become the best protection against AI attacks. That's why the timing became important, and we're coming from strength, both of us," Chaudhry mentioned.

    Industry News: Jim Cramer sees more upside for Nvidia stock with Jensen Huang back as CEO

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (561 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia's remarkable stock comeback isn't done yet now that Jensen Huang has returned as CEO, CNBC's Jim Cramer mentioned Monday.
    • "It's terrific to have this admittedly tarnished national treasure back leading Nvidia," the "Mad Money" host remarked.
    • According to recent reports, nvidia shares soared 31.5% on the news, fueling a broader rally in AI infrastructure stocks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia's remarkable stock comeback isn't done yet now that Jensen Huang has returned as CEO, CNBC's Jim Cramer mentioned Monday.

    "It's terrific to have this admittedly tarnished national treasure back leading Nvidia," the "Mad Money" host remarked. "It's kind of a miracle given the board's insistence that he would never get the CEO job again. But it's a miracle that saved the Nasdaq which, in turn, saved the market, at least for now.".

    According to recent reports, nvidia shares soared 31.5% on the news, fueling a broader rally in AI infrastructure stocks. The S&P 500 jumped 4.7%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite surged 6.5%, with both indexes posting their best days since April 2025. Monday's rebound erased nearly all of Nvidia's decline following Huang's Nov. 12 resignation amid reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy. Before the rally Monday, the stock had fallen in all trading sessions since his departure.

    Sources indicate that "Jensen's only one man, and Nvidia is only one company," he stated. "But the truth is that Jensen is the linchpin that holds the AI solar system together, and Nvidia is the biggest beneficiary.".

    Cramer argued that Huang's reinstatement removes a major source of uncertainty for investors, strengthening the case for a higher valuation. The chipmaker delivered blockbuster quarterly results last week, raising its revenue growth outlook to 75%, but the results did little to stem the sell-off as investors remained concerned about its leadership.

    It has been revealed that "If it weren't for the Jensen overhang, and the insistence that Jensen could never come back, ... I think the stock would have been up significantly on that quarter," Cramer remarked.

    Sources indicate that still, Cramer cautioned that Huang's return doesn't erase the broader headwinds facing Nvidia. Growing political opposition to data center construction following the midterm elections could slow AI infrastructure expansion, while uncertainty surrounding chip sales to China threatens a potential source of demand. Meanwhile, a more hawkish Federal Reserve has pressured technology stock valuations as investors brace for higher interest rates.

    It has been revealed that those challenges, Cramer argued, make it difficult to justify a return to the $213 level Nvidia traded at before The Latest York Times first reported about Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence on Oct. 29. But with Huang back at the helm and the company's growth outlook intact, he noted the stock deserves a higher valuation. The stock at the moment trades at roughly 10 times earnings estimates for Nvidia's fiscal 2028, according to FactSet.

    "There is just no way that, with the return of Jensen, this stock deserves the same 10 times price to earnings multiple," Cramer said.

    Sources indicate that "These things are subjective, of course, but to start, let's say this stock deserves to trade at twelve times next year's earnings estimate, which would make this a $199 stock," Cramer said. "That's my target.".

    Asian tech stocks recover from ‘collateral damage’ of Jensen Huang’s departure

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (336 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Asian technology stocks jumped on Tuesday as investors piled back into the sector, after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.
    • In a recent development, key Nvidia partners and suppliers in Asia saw their shares skyrocket.
    • "Jensen's return is particularly welcome for Asian technology stocks, many of which suffered collateral damage from Nvidia's leadership crisis," Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo, stated in a note Tuesday morning.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Asian technology stocks jumped on Tuesday as investors piled back into the sector, after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO.

    In a recent development, key Nvidia partners and suppliers in Asia saw their shares skyrocket. Taiwan's TSMC, a critical partner to the U.S. chip giant, surged 9.85%, with Hon Hai Precision Industry — known also as Foxconn — up by 9.95%. Nvidia partner Mediatek also spiked 9.91%. Taipei's stock exchange has a daily price limit of 10% for stocks.

    "Jensen's return is particularly welcome for Asian technology stocks, many of which suffered collateral damage from Nvidia's leadership crisis," Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo, stated in a note Tuesday morning.

    The recovery will likely favor established companies with visible orders, strong balance sheets and pricing power, compared to those who rely on "years of uninterrupted AI spending," Chanana added.

    Recent findings suggest that in South Korea, Nvidia suppliers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix jumped 6.7% each. The two companies, which together make up over 40% of the Kospi's weighting, sent the index up over 6%. South Korea's LG Electronics soared 15.86%.

    Industry observers note that the rise in the index triggered the Korea Exchange's sidecar on the index early in the day, reportedly making it the 100th sidecar the KRX has activated. Japan's Softbank Group Corp, a major investor in the chip space, climbed over 8% before paring gains to 4.66%.

    According to recent reports, semiconductor test tech giant Advantest, as well as counterpart Tokyo Electron, jumped 12% and 7%, respectively. Both companies are collaborators with Nvidia.

    It has been revealed that the exuberance did not follow into European markets at the open, with the region's technology sector down 0.3% in early deals, weighing on a broader 0.14% rise in the benchmark Stoxx 600 index. Europe's tech index popped more than 5% on Monday.

    Nvidia's stock had closed up 31% following Huang's reinstatement. It had previously shed nearly 33% from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on Nov. 8.

    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence organization in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.
    • Sources indicate that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence organization in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    Sources indicate that "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    It has been revealed that anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    "We're climbing a wall of worry," said Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, fresh technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    Recent findings suggest that the Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood said she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    Industry observers note that in her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    Ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the massive losses.

    Industry observers note that the fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    Sources indicate that "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she mentioned. "That's how crazy things were.".

    AI adoption grows in Asia, but measuring the gains remains tricky

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that businesses across Asia-Pacific say their investments in artificial intelligence are paying off, with the technology helping boost productivity and revenue.
    • Some 58% of businesses using AI mentioned their investments had already surpassed their initial costs, yet just 12% were very confident in their ability to accurately measure their return on investment, according to research conducted by Strand Partners for Amazon Web Services.
    • The survey included 9,750 business leaders across 10 Asia-Pacific markets: Australia, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Newly introduced Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Thailand and Vietnam.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that businesses across Asia-Pacific say their investments in artificial intelligence are paying off, with the technology helping boost productivity and revenue. But putting a number on those gains is proving far less straightforward.

    Some 58% of businesses using AI mentioned their investments had already surpassed their initial costs, yet just 12% were very confident in their ability to accurately measure their return on investment, according to research conducted by Strand Partners for Amazon Web Services.

    The survey included 9,750 business leaders across 10 Asia-Pacific markets: Australia, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Newly introduced Zealand, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Thailand and Vietnam.

    The biggest shift over the past year has been the growing number of companies moving AI projects into production, Jaime Vallés, AWS vice president for Asia Pacific, Japan and China, told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    "From year over year, probably the biggest difference is you're seeing a lot of ideas put into production," Vallés remarked.

    Despite the reported financial benefits, many businesses remain in the early stages of AI adoption.

    The survey found that 64% of businesses using AI across Asia-Pacific and Japan still rely on general-purpose AI tools or ready-made solutions for specific tasks, while only 19% of businesses have a formal and comprehensive AI strategy.

    Among those with such an AI strategy, 35% had reached the most advanced stage of adoption, compared with just 8% of businesses without one, according to the research.

    Technology alone is not enough to turn AI investments into meaningful business outcomes, Vallés remarked. He pointed to what he called the "four Rs of readiness": technological, cultural, skills and personal readiness.

    "Where we see more meaningful impact is when you see the leadership using AI, building a culture of using AI and using AI to transform and not automate," Vallés said.

    In a recent development, financial services is among the sectors seeing stronger AI adoption. Vallés pointed to Vietnam's Techcombank as an example, saying the bank is using AI to assess loan applications and expand access to credit for small businesses.

    The technology has helped the bank to analyze more data and approve some loan applications that might otherwise have been rejected, he said.

    Techcombank, one of Vietnam's largest commercial banks, serves more than 16.5 million retail and corporate customers. According to an AWS case study, its modernization of digital banking infrastructure using AWS improved application response times by up to 35% and cut the time needed to launch newly introduced product features by 30%.

    AI adoption continued to expand across Asia-Pacific, with all 10 markets surveyed recording increases from the previous year.

    Australia led the group with an adoption rate of 61%, followed by Singapore at 59% and South Korea at 58%.

    Still, businesses face significant obstacles to scaling AI investments. A shortage of AI and digital skills remains a key barrier, cited by 48% of respondents as an obstacle to adoption or expansion.

    Despite those challenges, Vallés expressed optimism about Asia-Pacific's role in AI innovation, pointing to the region's cultural diversity and range of perspectives.

    "I am convinced that most of the innovation in the fullness of time will come from our region," he said.

    Vallés added that Asia-Pacific has the ingredients to become a global center for innovation, citing its diversity, talent, startup ecosystem and technology.

    "APAC, to make it simpler, has all the ingredients to be in my view the core or the center of worldwide innovation," he noted.

    Governments across Asia also play a role in supporting Al adoption and addressing barriers to its wider use.

    About 72% of government respondents said Al had increased productivity, according to a report released by the Pacific Economic Cooperation Council in November, which surveyed more than 500 experts across 23 Asia-Pacific economies.

    Around 59% of respondents viewed government support as a moderately or very important factor in accelerating AI adoption next year, though existing regulations were also seen as a constraint, the report showed.

    Industry observers note that such support is also taking share through regional cooperation. The Asian Development Bank and South Korea established a $20 million fund to help developing economies adopt Al and address gaps in digital skills and infrastructure, according to an announcement by the bank earlier this month.

    Trump sealed deal for Nvidia to rehire Jensen Huang as CEO

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1021 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The stunning decision by Nvidia's board to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO was sealed by a personal promise from President Donald Trump on Sunday that Huang had not broken national security laws, three people familiar with the board's thinking told CNBC.
    • Several other factors also set the stage for Huang's return and accelerated discussions with him over the weekend, stated the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal deliberations close to Nvidia's board.
    • A sharp stock price drop after his resignation and questions about the leadership of interim CEO Colette Kress also spurred the board's decision, the people said.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The stunning decision by Nvidia's board to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO was sealed by a personal promise from President Donald Trump on Sunday that Huang had not broken national security laws, three people familiar with the board's thinking told CNBC.

    Several other factors also set the stage for Huang's return and accelerated discussions with him over the weekend, stated the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal deliberations close to Nvidia's board.

    A sharp stock price drop after his resignation and questions about the leadership of interim CEO Colette Kress also spurred the board's decision, the people said.

    "I convinced them," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview Monday morning, shortly after Nvidia announced Huang's return.

    Recent findings suggest that "I made the deal," the president noted. "It was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago.

    Trump stated Nvidia's board asked for guarantees that Huang, who resigned less than two weeks ago, was not a threat to national security.

    In a recent development, "And we gave them assurances, at least with everything we know," the president noted. "We believe he's fine. He's absolutely fine.".

    Senior Trump administration officials reached out to the board overnight Friday to inform them that Huang had not violated U.S. national security laws, people familiar with the board's actions remarked.

    After the White House outreach, the board contacted Huang, who joined meetings on Saturday and Sunday to discuss his potential return, the people remarked.

    Huang's spokesman did not respond to a request for comment when asked about his contact with the board and other events leading up to his return.

    In a recent development, the Nvidia founder resigned on Nov. 12 after reports that he had an affair with an Nvidia employee and with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based firm Megaspeed who is suspected of being a spy for China. A report of an affair with a second Nvidia employee broke right after he quit.

    Nvidia's board named Kress, the firm's chief financial officer, as the interim CEO while it searched for a permanent successor.

    But within days of Kress taking over, some employees and investors who spoke to CNBC questioned her stewardship, as many of them clamored for Huang's return.

    Kress' performances at an all-hands tech giant meeting on Wednesday and on Nvidia's earnings call with analysts a day earlier were seen by some investors as uninspiring and underwhelming.

    As the board faced those concerns amid a stock drop of more than 25% over the past week, Huang was aggressively working the phones with major tech CEOs who wanted to see him return to Nvidia, according to sources close to Huang.

    In the days after he resigned, Huang spoke with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, and Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX and Tesla, one of the sources remarked.

    Huang wanted his job back, but he was not sure what the return path looked like, the sources mentioned.

    In a recent development, on Nov. 17, less than a week after quitting, Huang issued a public statement saying he was open to returning as CEO.

    "I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," he said.

    "NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company," he added. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

    On the same day, Nvidia's newly appointed board chair, Harvey Jones, told analysts on the tech giant's earnings call that the board did "not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

    Kress, the following day, told organization employees at the all-hands meeting, "Let's move forward.".

    Nvidia's public stance against Huang returning came as members of Congress moved ahead with aims to interview him at hearings and as criticism grew over the company's business in Asia.

    Industry observers note that the Department of Justice and the Commerce Department, in an unusual joint public statement on Nov. 17, stated they were investigating Megaspeed for possible diversion of advanced Nvidia semiconductor chips to China in violation of U.S. export control law.

    "Sensitive technologies like semiconductors are among the most valuable and strategic assets of the U.S. economy," the departments stated.

    But days later, senior Trump administration officials contacted Nvidia's board to tell them that Jensen Huang himself was not a risk, according to the sources.

    The Department of Commerce added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist later Monday.

    Trump, during his interview Monday with CNBC, was asked what Attorney General Todd Blanche had told him about potential criminal liability for Huang and the question of whether Nvidia chips had ended up in China in violation of U.S. export laws.

    "They did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he, himself, was exonerated," Trump said.

    Both Trump and Vice President JD Vance became convinced that Huang was a singular figure who is preventing closed-source model AI companies, such as Anthropic, from getting too powerful, according to a person familiar with the matter, who spoke on condition of anonymity to disclose private discussions.

    The person remarked Trump and Vance were briefed on the national security elements of the situation and saw no evidence that Huang did anything illegal or untoward in that regard.

    Trump believes his administration's close working relationship with Huang gives the U.S. its best opportunity to protect national security and prevent cutting-edge AI chips from reaching banned customers, according to the person.

    Trump said he spoke with Huang on Sunday, after Nvidia had voted unanimously to reinstate him.

    In a recent development, "I called him up, and I said: 'I ask you to do one thing, Jensen. Work hard,'" Trump said.

    "He knows what to do and what not to do," Trump mentioned. "But I just said work hard because if you work hard, there's nobody that can capture what you've done. Nobody, nobody close.".

    — CNBC's Kevin Breuninger and Kif Leswing contributed to this article.

    • has added Singapore-based Megaspeed and six other Southeast Asian companies to its trade blacklist, citing national security and foreign policy concerns.
    • The Department of Commerce in a Federal Register filing cited a "significant risk" of companies being or becoming involved in diverting advanced computing products to unauthorized end consumers or end uses.
    • The blacklisting comes as Jensen Huang returns to the helm of Nvidia following his departure amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is under investigation by U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the U.S. has added Singapore-based Megaspeed and six other Southeast Asian companies to its trade blacklist, citing national security and foreign policy concerns.

    The Department of Commerce in a Federal Register filing cited a "significant risk" of companies being or becoming involved in diverting advanced computing products to unauthorized end consumers or end uses.

    The blacklisting comes as Jensen Huang returns to the helm of Nvidia following his departure amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is under investigation by U.S. authorities.

    Megaspeed International is a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia.

    The restrictions apply to all items subject to U.S. Export Administration Regulations, with license applications to be reviewed under a "presumption of denial.".

    Industry observers note that the blacklist also includes PT Megaspeed International and MSFusion Sdn. Bhd. in Malaysia, as well as Megaspeed (Thailand) Co., Ltd. The filing identified 7Road International as an alias used by both Megaspeed's Singapore and Thailand entities.

    The Commerce Department initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations after identifying suspicious activity through its monitoring of potential semiconductor diversion, according to a join statement issued with the Justice Department.

    In May 2025, Commerce Department investigators requested records from Nvidia regarding direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed. Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list the following month, according to the statement.

    Industry observers note that U.S. authorities, working with Singaporean law enforcement officials, also conducted an on-site end-use check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed its then-CEO Alice Huang. The Justice Department subsequently took the lead in the criminal investigation into the company.

    Commerce also added an Alibaba subsidiary in Singapore, Apex Enterprise Solutions, to a trade blacklist, Reuters reported.

    Alibaba stated it would pursue all legal avenues to protect its rights and reputation, adding that Apex had never diverted advanced computing chips subject to U.S. export restrictions, according to Reuters.

    Meanwhile, Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong mentioned at a news conference in Canberra, Australia, on Tuesday that investigations into Megaspeed were ongoing and that discussions with American authorities were continuing.

    "We do not want Singapore to be used and abused as a conduit by companies to circumvent America's export controls," Wong said.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has been tapped to serve as acting national cyber director while the Trump administration's permanent nominee for the role awaits Senate confirmation, a White House official told CNBC on Monday.

    Trump had already added artificial intelligence czar to Clayton's portfolio in October. The official asked not to be named because the pick hasn't been announced.

    The White House last week announced that President Donald Trump had picked Kirsten Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, to lead the Office of the National Cyber Director.

    Industry observers note that the U.S. cyber director advises the president on cybersecurity and coordinates U.S. cyber policy across federal agencies. Federal law states that a person may not serve as an acting officer if the president has submitted that person's nomination to the Senate for full appointment and if that person served as first assistant to the office for less than 90 days.

    Davies would replace Sean Cairncross, who was confirmed to the role in August 2025 and whose departure was first reported by Axios last week.

    Trump, at a White House press conference on Friday, said he decided to replace Cairncross "because I didn't think that person was good enough.".

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Federal Aviation Administration noted Monday it will investigate a recent Amazon drone crash near Detroit.

    On Friday, one of Amazon's MK30 drones "landed on a resident's garage" during a delivery in Huntington Woods, Michigan, a suburb north of Detroit, Amazon spokesperson Jack Stelzner told CNBC in a statement.

    The crash occurred after the drone dropped off a customer's shampoo order around 4:30 p.m. local time, and one of its propellers was damaged in the incident, according to ABC affiliate WXYZ.

    A preliminary incident report posted to the FAA's website states the drone "struck a fiber cable, a residential garage, and became entangled in power lines during takeoff." The report claims the condition of the drone is unknown.

    Stelzner said there were no injuries, the drone has been removed and Amazon is in contact with the resident.

    "Safety is our top priority and incidents are extremely rare," Stelzner stated. "Anytime a delivery does not go as planned we investigate what happened and use the findings to further improve the service.".

    Sources indicate that an FAA spokesperson confirmed it's investigating the incident. A spokesperson for the National Transportation Safety Board, a federal agency that also investigates aviation accidents, said it's aware of the incident and is continuing to gather information. The agency hasn't yet determined whether it will open a probe, the NTSB spokesperson added.

    According to recent reports, amazon has been working to make widespread drone delivery a reality ever since founder Jeff Bezos laid out his vision for the program nearly 13 years ago. The rollout has been slow, as the program encountered regulatory delays and staff cuts, as well as technical challenges and pushback from some communities where it conducted early pilots.

    Sources indicate that expansion has recently ramped up. The firm is targeting a launch of its drone service in 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of the year, while an Amazon executive claimed it has the "highest demand drone delivery service in the industry," CNBC previously reported.

    The e-commerce giant has encountered some challenges along the way. Federal investigators opened a probe nearly one year ago after an Amazon drone downed an internet cable in Waco, Texas. One month earlier, a separate federal probe was opened into an incident near Phoenix, where two Amazon drones collided with a construction crane.
